B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP access price or MCP-specific limit is published. Fin Operator message calls use Operator credits in the same way as turns started in Intercom; the other four Operator tools are free.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page lists Essential from $19 per seat/month billed annually (or $29 monthly), Advanced $85 per seat/month, and Expert $132 per seat/month. Fin AI Agent is listed from $0.99 per outcome. Pro, which includes Operator, is listed from $100/month.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Fin AI Agent is priced per outcome. Operator calls through send_operator_message consume Operator credits; the Fin Operator guide describes the same usage as a turn started in Intercom. Other four Fin Operator tools are free. The pricing page notes usage-based charges for some channels.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: US and EU hosted workspaces are supported; AU is not. Fin Operator tools require a Fin Operator workspace, OAuth connection, teammate Operator permission, and Use Fin Operator permission. The OAuth redirect URI must be allowlisted, except localhost and 127.0.0.1 callbacks, which are permitted on any port. Fin Operator calls are limited to 60 per minute per connection.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Intercom controls hosted-region availability and redirect-URI allowlisting; workspace administrators and teammate permissions determine product access; the connecting user authorizes the connection.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="OAuth", error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing or invalid access token", resource_metadata="https://mcp.intercom.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", scope="mcp operator". The supplied protected-resource documents report resource values https://mcp.intercom.com and https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp, authorization server https://mcp.intercom.com, scopes_supported ["mcp", "operator"], and bearer_methods_supported ["header"]. Authorization-server metadata reports issuer https://mcp.intercom.com, authorization endpoint /authorize, token endpoint /token, registration endpoint /register, scopes_supported ["mcp", "operator"], response_types_supported ["code"], response_modes_supported ["query"], grant_types_supported ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["client_secret_basic", "client_secret_post", "none"], revocation_endpoint /token, and code_challenge_methods_supported ["S256"]. The guide documents OAuth and bearer-token authentication, dynamic client registration, redirect URI allowlisting, and localhost exceptions. Token lifetime is not stated. The guide says product permissions are checked for tool use.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Authentication failure at the supplied endpoint returns HTTP 401 with a JSON invalid_token error and the WWW-Authenticate metadata described above.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc / Dynamic Client Registration / bearer token: OAuth authorization_code and refresh_token grants; PKCE S256; token endpoint authentication methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none; scopes_supported: mcp, operator; bearer method header. DCR endpoint https://mcp.intercom.com/register. Revocation endpoint https://mcp.intercom.com/token. Guide documents OAuth consent and direct bearer-token authentication. Token lifetime not found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. Official guide lists read tools, article creation/update, and add_internal_note. Fin Operator tools include proposal application and rejection. Only the Fin Operator guide publishes annotations; it explicitly says annotations are hints, not enforcement. The core 14 tools' annotations are not documented.
2. The Fin Operator workflow recommends reviewing proposals and human confirmation before apply; apply_proposals itself accepts proposals and has no documented confirm parameter. The guide says some changes cannot be undone. No server-enforced confirmation flag is documented. Operator may separately wait for teammate input/confirmation in Intercom.
3. OAuth metadata supports scopes mcp and operator; docs describe product permissions for conversations, contacts/companies, articles, and Use Fin Operator. Operator permissions inherit teammate access. Fin Operator requires OAuth and is unavailable with bearer tokens. Redirect URIs are allowlisted; localhost/127.0.0.1 callbacks are allowed on any port. Token lifetime was not found.
4. US and EU endpoints are documented; AU workspaces are unsupported. Legacy SSE is deprecated. No read-only mode, toolsets filter, or query-free mode is documented. Fin Operator tools are conditional on workspace, OAuth, and permission.
5. No general PII masking or field-exclusion mechanism is documented. add_internal_note is teammate-only and cannot send customer-visible replies; note authorship is fixed to the authorizing admin. EU endpoint processing is documented as within the EU.
6. Search/list pagination is documented, commonly up to 150 results per page; list_companies caps per_page at 60; list_articles allows 1–150. Fin proposal detail responses are about 1 MB and describe at most 50 proposals at a time; apply_proposals allows 5 proposals per call and reject_proposals 20 IDs. Fin Operator calls are limited to 60 per minute per connection. No general MCP rate limit is stated. Operator message calls consume Operator credits.
7. Search validates fields and operators and returns errors for invalid queries. add_internal_note normalizes supported conversation ID forms. Docs state required parameters and some constraints; implementation-level unknown-argument handling and coercion are not documented.
8. Server logging, audit trails, and MCP telemetry are not described in the reviewed guides.
9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report-to-vendor tool appears in the official lists. No MCP upsell response or marketing elicitation is documented. Fin Operator uses credits; pricing separately lists Fin outcomes and Pro.
10. Server-side instructions or skills are not published in the reviewed guides. Behavioral recommendations include checking proposal changes and not re-sending a possibly accepted Operator message. The server's enforcement of these recommendations is not documented.
11. Operator chats retain current turn state and proposals for later retrieval via chat_id. No effect of prior independent agent behavior on future tool availability is documented.
12. The main endpoint has a flat documented list with five conditional Fin Operator tools. The Fin Operator tools invoke Intercom's separate Operator agent within the workspace; a separate Fin Agent API MCP endpoint is also documented as another server.
13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or equivalent universal escape-hatch tool is documented.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: [DOCS] “Once a turn has been accepted, never re-send the same message to retry.”
[DOCS] “Never starts new work and never waits — it returns the chat's current state immediately.”
[DOCS] “Review each one with get_proposal_details before you apply it — some changes cannot be undone.”
[DOCS] “Set it only when a human explicitly chose a mode, and only to a mode listed in that proposal's supported_apply_modes.”
[DOCS] “Quote numbers and data from tool_outputs verbatim rather than re-deriving them.”
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented tool set varies by workspace and authentication/permission conditions, and includes tools that delegate work to Fin Operator, a vendor agent operating inside Intercom. Intercom also documents separate regional endpoints and a separate Fin Agent API MCP endpoint.

E_aggregated.token_method: No deployed server implementation or verbatim initialize/tool definitions were available. Official guides document tool descriptions and partial parameters, not the complete serialized tool definitions and initialize instructions required for the specified character-count method.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The main MCP guide documents tools for searching and retrieving conversations/contacts, company and Help Center article operations, and internal notes; it does not document customer-visible conversation replies, ticket operations, or general workspace administration. Fin Operator proposals can include broader configuration changes, but only through the separate Operator workflow. Intercom's REST API documents a broader API surface; this study did not treat REST-only operations as MCP tools. Sources: https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp ; https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/fin-operator-mcp ; https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The guide recommends reviewing proposal details before applying and requires a human to choose apply_mode when overriding a proposal's default. It states: “Review each one with get_proposal_details before you apply it — some changes cannot be undone.” The guide describes tool annotations as client hints and explicitly says authorization decides whether calls are allowed. The main guide advises checking the OAuth redirect address and cancelling if the app or destination is not recognized.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Intercom states that authentication verifies user permissions and that access is authenticated and authorized. The EU endpoint is stated to process requests within the EU in line with Regional Data Hosting commitments. The guide says internal notes are visible to teammates only and cannot send customer-visible replies. The reviewed pages do not specify MCP-specific retention, AI training, audit logging, or field masking terms.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The main guide presents MCP as a standardized, secure way for AI clients to access Intercom data. The Fin Operator guide says proposals can be reviewed and applied from the client and that the read-only proposal-details tool costs no Operator credits.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Authentication and product permission checks are documented as access controls. Proposal application is a separate tool from proposal review, but the human-review guidance is described as workflow advice rather than an enforced confirmation parameter. Tool annotations are explicitly hints. The EU processing statement is a regional hosting promise; no corresponding MCP-specific retention, masking, or audit mechanism is documented.

contradictions: The public repository README describes an older six-tool server and US-only support; the current official hosted MCP guide describes 14 core tools plus five conditional Fin Operator tools and supports US and EU. The repository copy does not contain implementation code, so the difference may reflect documentation age rather than deployed-code behavior.

The Claude connector directory lists six tools, while the current official guide lists 14 core tools. The Claude listing is a third-party connector directory entry and does not include the article, company, or note tools documented by Intercom.

OAuth metadata advertises scopes_supported ["mcp", "operator"], while the guide describes consent permissions for conversations, contacts/companies, articles, and Use Fin Operator. The metadata scopes are not a one-to-one enumeration of those product permissions.
Composio's intercom toolkit pages show platform toolkit counts (including 133 and 15), not a confirmed native tool list for the input endpoint; these counts were excluded from actions.
observations_for_research: The Fin Operator tools are exposed conditionally by workspace capability, OAuth use, and teammate permission; bearer-token connections do not receive them.

Proposal review, application, and rejection are separate tools. The documentation differentiates tool annotation hints from permission enforcement and describes review/confirmation as a human workflow.
Fin Operator delegates work to Intercom's internal agent and returns asynchronous status, clarifying questions, and proposed changes through separate retrieval tools.
